evidence.excerpt: `Application#stop()` requires you to have an application instance. If an exception is thrown before the app is initialized, you may still have some resources to free.
evidence.interpretation: gmethvin challenged a lifecycle redesign that would make cleanup depend on successful application construction. The author retained independently reachable lifecycle handling; this is not a claim that all partial-initialization leaks were eliminated.
evidence.author: gmethvin

evidence.excerpt: The Play application depends on the `ActorSystem` (at least the way it's set up right now), so `Play.stop` should invoke `CoordinatedShutdown` and not the other way around.
evidence.interpretation: gmethvin identified the dependency direction behind a shutdown self-wait. Later author discussion distinguished shared production ActorSystems from separate development systems; a merge is not proof of every shutdown path.
evidence.author: gmethvin

evidence.excerpt: At the very least, it seems like it shouldn't happen concurrently with the `"user-provided-server-stop-hook"` task above, but because `CoordinatedShutdown` does not sequence tasks linearly, they will run concurrently unless you explicitly `flatMap` the tasks or put them into different phases.
evidence.interpretation: TimMoore requested an explicit ordering edge rather than relying on same-phase registration order. The 2020 source still places two tasks in the same phase, so this is reviewer guidance, not a proven repository-wide invariant.
evidence.author: TimMoore

evidence.excerpt: I'd not use `Duration.Inf` because that would result in the worst kind error handling if there is a problem -- complete silence and hanging process.
evidence.interpretation: patriknw defended a bounded outer wait after the phase budget, and gmethvin later requested an explanatory comment. The numerical five-second margin is historical policy, not a universal timeout recommendation.
evidence.author: patriknw

evidence.excerpt: Also please look at the last two commits, where I fixed the initialization of the reloader because in original scala code these were lazy vars, so they should come after the "before started" hooks, otherwise file watcher would already run (and the `assetsClassLoader` function would be processed, which could be anything set by the user).
evidence.interpretation: Although the review state is APPROVED, this excerpt contains substantive reasoning and an implementation correction by mkurz. It is dated December 2023; the surviving rebased head and correction commits are March 2024.
evidence.author: mkurz

evidence.excerpt: Yes, I saw it. It's my fault while migrating from lazy vars, sorry

evidence.interpretation: Source observation: an AtomicBoolean gates hook execution, a Promise memoizes completion, and hooks are chained using flatMap. Synchronous hook throws and failed futures are recovered; this is Future-based lifecycle code, not a Cats Effect or ZIO resource API.

Source observation: tests assert reverse registration order, continuation after thrown and asynchronous failures, and one hook invocation across repeated stop calls. Repeated sequential calls are not a deterministic simultaneous-call race test.

Source observation: termination delegates fallback parsing to CoordinatedShutdown and uses binding.terminate rather than only unbind. HTTP then HTTPS are awaited sequentially, and logger/user hooks later occupy the same phase: avoid asserting parallel termination or complete dependency ordering.

Source observation: scripted integration starts a slow request, signals production termination, and checks the recorded body. Sleeps are used to stage the historical test, so it is not a deterministic proof of every shutdown interleaving.

Source observation: the hook runner appears before assetsClassLoader.apply and eager DevServerReloader construction. The source also has a repeated-run guard, onError handling and a close path, but these facts alone do not prove leak freedom on every failure path.

Source observation: plugin unit tests deliberately inspect the wrapped original cause after the Java port and also inspect composite failures. This is not a direct test of watcher initialization ordering; the latter remains a peer-evaluation extension.

Source observation: the 2020 build separates core, web filters, transport backends, testkit and dev tooling. The actual sbt project ID is Filters-Helpers, not the Scala val name; integration tests are in IntegrationTest, and scripted support is another test layer.

Source observation: the 2022 integration project still uses IntegrationTest with non-publication and both Akka HTTP and Netty dependencies. A 2024 Test selector cannot simply be applied to this snapshot.

Source observation: by December 2024 the filter ID has the Play prefix; the integration project uses Test and Pekko HTTP replaces Akka HTTP in this tree. Run support is a non-cross-built Java boundary, and Play-Configuration is separated from Play core.

Source observation: the December 2020 snapshot pins Akka HTTP 10.1.13 and defaults Akka to 2.6.10. These are snapshot defaults, not assertions about the January 2020 PR head or every Play 2.8 release.

Source observation: the December 2022 snapshot defaults Akka HTTP to 10.2.10 and Akka to 2.6.20, with system-property overrides. This is a JVM Future/Akka Streams line rather than an effect-polymorphic migration.

Source observation: the 2024 tree declares runtime-era Scala 2.13.15 and Scala 3.3.4 versions alongside Scala 2.12.20 for sbt-related work. Exact supported cross-build membership still depends on each project plugin.

Source observation: the December 2024 tree defaults Pekko to 1.0.3 and Pekko HTTP to 1.0.1. Porting a historical Akka snippet requires resolving this namespace and dependency boundary, not a blind current-source substitution.

Source observation: scripted dependency setup is intentionally disabled. The adjacent comments require prior local publication by the repository scripts; running scripted alone can test missing or stale artifacts.

claims.rule: When refactoring Play lifecycle wiring, preserve cleanup reachability before Application construction succeeds and preserve lazy acquisition relative to startup hooks; reject a rewrite that requires an Application instance to clean up partially allocated resources.
claims.applicability: Observed Play JVM Future/DI and Java-port review practice across 2018 and 2023-2024. Inference: an event trace should show beforeStarted preceding file-watcher and user asset-loader activation; this is not an instruction to replace the chosen effect model.
claims.counterexample: A plain immutable configuration value has no resource acquisition or user callback, so moving its initialization earlier is not automatically a lifecycle defect.

claims.rule: For a stop refactor, distinguish one invocation from one completion signal: all callers should observe the actual final completion, hooks should remain LIFO and sequential, and one failed hook must not silently skip later cleanup.
claims.applicability: Inference from DefaultApplicationLifecycle and explicit shutdown-order review. Same-phase CoordinatedShutdown tasks are not ordered by registration; the 2020 server snapshot is a counterexample to claiming the requested logger ordering was fully implemented.
claims.counterexample: Independent same-phase tasks may intentionally execute concurrently. A request-scoped operation also must not be forced into a global memoized once-only lifecycle merely because both return Future.

claims.rule: A graceful server-stop change must distinguish listener unbinding from completion of in-flight responses and retain a finite failure-observable shutdown budget; verify the configured fallback through the owning shutdown API.
claims.applicability: Observed Akka HTTP Play 2.8.x repair in PR 9970 plus 2018 timeout discussion. Inference: separately test deadline expiration, HTTP/HTTPS combination and streaming responses; the examined scripted test covers only a staged successful slow request.
claims.counterexample: A listener-only administrative unbind may deliberately leave existing requests running. Do not replace such an API with full termination without establishing ownership and its public contract.

claims.rule: Derive test project IDs, configurations and scripted prerequisites from the pinned build before proposing validation; use actual unit, integration and plugin consumers instead of assuming that one test command covers the change.
claims.applicability: Inference from historical sbt organization. Runtime Future and Akka/Pekko Streams choices remain intact, Java build-link boundaries are not evidence for migrating the whole framework to Java, and no upstream build is executed by this research run.
claims.counterexample: Sbt-Plugin/scripted does not replace Sbt-Plugin/test. Using a 2024 Test selector for a 2020 IntegrationTest suite or assuming the old Filters-Helpers ID in the 2024 tree can omit the intended tests.
